rule_text: For 18U, Babe Ruth League baseball rules (baberuthleague.org/documents/RulesBaseball.pdf) apply, except where these house rules say otherwise.

rule_text: All 10U and 13U bats must be USA Bats (USABat) or wood bats.

rule_text: All 18U bats must be BBCOR drop-3 or wood. Players age 14 may also use a USA (USABat) drop-5 bat.

rule_text: No cleats or spikes are allowed on the artificial turf at Sunshine Ballpark. Sneakers or turf shoes only.

rule_text: No bubble gum or sunflower seeds on the field or in the dugout at Sunshine Ballpark, because gum and seeds are hard to remove from artificial turf. Only clear Gatorade in the dugouts: Gatorade dye damages the turf.

rule_text: The third base dugout is the home dugout. Always.

keywords: dugout home visitor first base side which
rule_text: The first base dugout is the home dugout. Always.

keywords: late arrive arrives arrival shows show up absent missing lineup bottom out bat bats batting order
rule_text: A player who arrives late is added to the bottom of the lineup, but not until they arrive. If a player is in the lineup and has not shown up, it is an out the first time that spot comes up, and the player is removed from the lineup. If the player then arrives, they are added to the bottom of the lineup on arrival.

keywords: lineup batting order continuous everyone bats bench dugout change
rule_text: Every player present in the dugout must be in the batting lineup, and the batting order may not change.

keywords: defense playing time innings substitution sub free minimum bench field
rule_text: Players may move in and out on defense freely. Every player must play at least two innings on defense; they do not have to be consecutive innings.

keywords: injured injury hurt leave early ejected ejection removed out penalty
rule_text: A player who is injured or must leave a game early is removed from the lineup with no penalty. If a player is ejected, an automatic out is called each time their spot in the lineup comes up.

keywords: eight 8 players seven 7 forfeit minimum start short
rule_text: Games may start with eight players. If a team drops to seven players during the game, it is a forfeit.

keywords: pitch count pitches limit daily maximum rest days
rule_text: Pitch counts: 10U may throw 75 pitches a day; 13U may throw 85 pitches a day. Rest for 10U and 13U: 1-20 pitches, 0 days; 21-35, 1 day; 36-50, 2 days; 51-65, 3 days; 66 or more, 4 days.

keywords: pitch count pitches limit daily maximum rest days 105
rule_text: 18U pitch limit is 105 pitches. Rest: 76-105 pitches, 3 days; 51-75, 2 days; 26-50, 1 day. A pitcher with 25 or fewer pitches needs no rest day and can pitch the next day.
note: Board clarification 2026-10-24: 25 pitches or fewer needs no rest.

keywords: innings length long time limit six 6 hour
rule_text: 10U and 13U games are six innings. No new inning begins after 1 hour 45 minutes. The last inning will be called at the top of the inning no earlier than 1 hour 30 minutes of game play.

keywords: innings length long time limit seven 7 hours playoffs
rule_text: 18U games are seven innings. No new inning begins after 2 hours 15 minutes; in the playoffs the limit is 2 hours 30 minutes.

keywords: mound distance bases feet field size 46 60
rule_text: 10U field: 46-foot mound, 60-foot bases.

keywords: mound distance bases feet field size 50 70
rule_text: 13U field: 50-foot mound, 70-foot bases.

keywords: dropped uncaught third strike 3rd run first advance
rule_text: 10U: the batter cannot advance on a dropped third strike.

keywords: dropped uncaught third strike 3rd run first advance outs occupied
rule_text: 13U: on a dropped third strike the batter can run to first with fewer than 2 outs only if first base is unoccupied. With 2 outs, the batter can run to first whether or not first base is occupied.

keywords: steal stealing lead leading off home wild pitch passed ball advance bag
rule_text: 10U: no leading off; when the pitcher is on the mound the runner must be on the bag. Stealing is allowed at every base except from third to home. No stealing home, and no advancing on a wild pitch, a passed ball, an error on the catcher's routine throw back to the pitcher, or the pitcher dropping the ball on the mound. If the pitcher or catcher tries to put out the runner on third (or any other runner), the runner on third may try to score. Why: a more competitive game, no easy runs, faster pace, and games won by earned runs rather than errors by a young, inexperienced age group.

keywords: steal stealing lead leading off home wild pitch passed ball advance bag
rule_text: 13U: no leading off; when the pitcher is on the mound the runner must stay on the bag until the ball reaches the plate. Stealing second, third or home, and advancing on wild pitches and passed balls, is allowed after the pitch reaches home plate.

keywords: slide sliding headfirst head first dive pickoff
rule_text: 10U and 13U: no head-first sliding, except diving back to a base on a pick-off play.

keywords: slide sliding headfirst head first contact collision malicious ejection home plate
rule_text: 18U: runners may slide head-first into any base. Runners must slide and avoid contact with fielders at the bases and at home plate. Malicious contact is the umpire's judgment and results in immediate ejection.

keywords: warm up warmup pitches between innings pace
rule_text: 10U and 13U: 5 warm-up pitches (3 if the pitcher has already pitched more than 2 innings). Fewer if players take too long to get out of the dugout.
note: Board clarification 2026-10-24: 13U uses the same warm-up rule as 10U and 18U.

keywords: warm up warmup pitches between innings pace
rule_text: 18U: 5 warm-up pitches (3 if the pitcher has already pitched more than 2 innings). The umpire may reduce warm-up pitches to keep the pace of play.

keywords: five 5 run rule runs inning cap limit last inning unlimited
rule_text: Five-run rule: each inning ends when a team has scored five runs, except the last inning. Both teams are unlimited in the last inning.

keywords: mercy run rule 10 ten runs ahead after innings
rule_text: Mercy rule for 10U and 13U: 10 runs after 4 innings, or after 3.5 innings if the home team is winning.

keywords: mercy run rule 10 ten runs ahead after innings
rule_text: Mercy rule for 18U: 10 runs after 5 innings, or after 4.5 innings if the home team is ahead.

keywords: strike zone strikes balls height small short tall umpire
rule_text: 10U and 13U strike zone: adjusted reasonably for the player's age and height, at the umpire's discretion.

keywords: strike zone strikes balls letters knees umpire
rule_text: 18U strike zone: from the letters to the knees and over the plate. Pitchers at 18U should be able to throw strikes.

keywords: taunt taunting trash talk remarks sportsmanship ejection ejected suspension warning arguing argue
rule_text: Sportsmanship is paramount in the Sunshine Baseball League. No taunting and no remarks directed personally at players on the other team. After one warning, players or coaches who taunt or argue with umpires will be ejected. Any ejection of a player or coach includes a suspension for the next game, which can be appealed to the league executive board.

keywords: umpire call question discuss approach argue dispute coach manager between innings
rule_text: If a call or rule is in question, the head coach or manager may ask the umpire if they may approach; discussing between innings is strongly recommended. The head umpire decides whether a play or call needs to be discussed during an inning. Only head coaches or managers may discuss calls with umpires.

keywords: coaches umpires example kids friendly approachable goals safe life lesson
rule_text: All coaches and umpires should be approachable, friendly and nice: we are setting an example for the kids, and that comes first. Coaches, parents and umpires all share the same goals: a safe game and life-lesson learning for the children playing baseball.

keywords: parents fans yell yelling booing polite behavior leave ban removed stands
rule_text: Parents and fans must be polite and show good sportsmanship. Coaches should calm fans down, never stir them up; doing so is cause for ejection, suspension and possible expulsion from the league. Parents and fans who do not behave may be asked to leave the ballpark, and repeated problems can lead to season-long or permanent bans.

keywords: parents coach coaching sidelines dugout volunteer instructions yelling
rule_text: Parents do not coach from the sidelines during games. Only players and approved coaches are allowed in the dugouts during games. Parents who want to coach should volunteer as coaches, not undermine the volunteers who do.

keywords: pool player players short shorthanded fill borrow extra gamechanger request
rule_text: Teams without enough players for a regular-season game can request pool players by emailing sunshinegamechanger@gmail.com. Pool players bat at the bottom of the lineup, may not pitch or catch, wear their own team jersey and hat, and are entered in GameChanger as pool player 1, pool player 2, and so on.
